CENTRAL MINE PLANNING & DESIGN INSTITUTE LIMITED (CMPDI)
GEOLOGICAL REPORT ON EXPLORATION FOR COAL - NORTH KARANPURA COALFIELD
1.0 INTRODUCTION & STRATIGRAPHY
The exploratory block covers an area of approximately 14.5 sq. km in the eastern part
of the North Karanpura basin. Regional drilling was conducted to delineate the disposition
of major coal seams belonging to the Barakar Formation. The sedimentary sequence comprises
coarse-to-medium grained feldspathic sandstones, carbonaceous shales, and workable coal seams.
2.0 COAL SEAM CHARACTERISTICS
Seam VII (Top): Average clean thickness 4.25 m. Roof: Medium grained sandstone. Floor: Carbonaceous shale.
Seam VI (Bottom): Average thickness 6.80 m. Inherent moisture: 4.2%, Ash: 24.8%, GCV: 5120 kcal/kg.
Borehole CM-101 encountered Seam VII at depth 112.4 m and Seam VI at depth 145.8 m.
